current: qip_edge::envelope::VerifiedEnvelope and qip_edge::policy::{VerifiedPolicy, VerifiedHalt} verify an HMAC-SHA256 (qip_core::hmac_sha256, ADR 0002's named in-tree hashing) under a symmetric key the cell shares with the centre — the same refuse-on-tamper/refuse-on-missing-signature shape the requirement asks for, but with a shared secret rather than a KMS asymmetric signature.
gap: No KMS asymmetric signature verification exists or can exist in-tree today: it needs an asymmetric primitive (ADR 0043 names this as one of three gaps no in-tree code may close) and the Google auth flow a KMS call needs, which ADR 0009 forbids writing in-tree. A shared symmetric key is a weaker trust boundary than the requirement's threat model (anyone who can write to the package's storage cannot be distinguished from KMS by a shared secret two parties both hold).
verification: backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/tests/cell.rs's four signature tests prove the permitted (HMAC) form's refusal behaviour today. The requirement's own four-refusal integration check (flipped byte, digest mismatch, unknown key, no signature) is satisfied for HMAC, not for KMS.
notes: Recorded in ADR 0099's conflict register C2 as needing a dependency record (an asymmetric-primitive class) weighed against the in-tree-only policy before this can move.

current: Outcomes do reach the central ledger, though not from the journal and not through a Fabric. Each exchange publishes a CellStateDelta whose orders, fills, refusals and crosses are incremental since the previous delta (qip-edge/src/mesh.rs:179-236), idempotent by the cell's own sequence. qip-api drains the delta inbox into Platform::ingest_cell_report on POST /cycle (qip-api/src/mesh.rs:1621), which settles reported fills into the centre's strategy books. The hash-chained journal itself goes only to the node's configured KeyValueStore via Cell::flush (StoreMirror), and nothing central reads it back.
evidence: backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/src/mesh.rs:33-41 (nothing on the uplink is spooled; the incremental half of a delta whose circuit is open is lost)
backend/crates/apps/qip-api/src/mesh.rs:1-40,1621 (MeshBackbone drains deltas into ingest_cell_report), opened from qip-api/src/main.rs:318-320

Telemetry and policy/model acknowledgements do not travel at all. The drain is a blocking call on the pass thread, not asynchronous. There is no Fabric and no path from it to the learning loop.
verification: qip-api/tests/mesh.rs proves fills a cell reports over a real CellUplink reach the centre's books and that a redelivered delta is ingested once. Needed: journal-driven drain through the Fabric with an outage-and-restore session proving every outcome, telemetry and acknowledgement record arrives once, in journal order, with no decision waiting.
notes: Directly downstream of REFLEX-011; cannot be built before an embedded Fabric client exists to drain into. verify: upgraded MISSING -> PARTIAL with implemented/tested/integrated true. The assessor described the delta as a summary only; it carries incremental orders, fills, refusals and crosses that qip-api ingests into the ledger from its composition root (qip-api/src/mesh.rs:1621, main.rs:318), tested by qip-api tests/mesh.rs:747 and :344. current: The simulated feed's wire (qip.simulated-depth.2) carries the venue publisher's own sequence number on every line and DepthDecoder reads it instead of numbering lines itself, so the cell's Sequencer sees a venue sequence in the one configuration a composition root runs. Cell::on_bytes journals each observation as GapDetected under its own leading word (gap:, reorder:, duplicate:, abandoned:), duplicates summed per stream per call. Three defects that made the control unable to fire are fixed: the decoder manufactured the sequence; the reset the sequencer synthesises for an abandoned gap was looked up by a derived instrument id and reached no book (Cell::reset_venue now resets every book at the venue and the feature state with it); and nothing told the sequencer the time, so a gap followed by silence was held for ever (Cell::work and Cell::on_bytes now poll the deadline). SimulatedFeed::publish rebuilds a stale book from the venue's whole depth rather than a difference.
evidence: backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/feed.rs (level_line, DepthDecoder reads the wire's sequence; SimulatedFeed::publish resynchronises a stale book)

Six mutations, each fired and was restored byte-for-byte: the decoder numbering lines itself; the reset never reaching a book; Cell::work never judging the deadline; the feed never rebuilding a stale book; duplicates dropped in silence; a recovered reorder not signalled.
notes: Closed 2026-10-04. The requirement's own replay check is met on the adapter the node runs. The decoders that read a real venue's sequence numbers (FIX MsgSeqNum, ITCH, SBE) still have no production caller: that is REFLEX-016, and each will owe the same replay when it is wired. After an abandoned gap every book at the venue is reset, not only the ones the lost sequences touched, because which those were is what was lost.

current: The one decoder a composition root reaches, the simulated feed's DepthDecoder, now writes the two timestamps from two sources: capture_time is the node's clock at receipt, and venue_time is read from the line, where the feed's publisher stamped the venue's own clock (SimulatedGateway::now). The decoder refuses a frame whose receipt instant is earlier than the last it stamped (invalid, nothing consumed, Diagnostics::frames_refused counted), so receipt stamps are monotonic within the adapter and a clock that ran backwards is refused rather than restamped.
verification: backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/feed.rs unit tests (both stamps on one decoded level, 3 ms apart; a backwards receipt refused) and backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/tests/sequence.rs through SimulatedFeed::publish. Two mutations, each fired and was restored byte-for-byte: venue_time written from the receipt stamp; a backwards receipt stamped anyway.
notes: Closed 2026-10-04. One frame is one receipt: the in-process venue hands a frame over whole, so every line of it shares the receipt instant. In a running node the venue's clock and the receipt instant are the same value, because run_pass advances the gateway to the pass instant before the feed publishes; that is what a venue with no wire between it and the cell measures, and the fields diverge wherever the two clocks do. The receipt clock is read once per pass, which is once per health probe until REFLEX-001's scheduler lands. FIX/ITCH/SBE decoders set distinct stamps already and remain unwired (REFLEX-016).

current: qip_edge::funding module holds funding-rate and borrow-availability state per instrument. FundingRate(Decimal) holds the decimal percentage per time period (positive=holder pays, negative=receiver). BorrowAvailability(Option<Decimal>) holds the quantity available to borrow or None if unknown/unavailable. FundingState manages two BTreeMaps keyed by instrument name, one per fact.
